question.text: Under the existing SEBI (AIF) Regulations, is appointing a custodian mandatory for all AIFs?

answer.text: Only mandatory for Category III AIFs dealing in listed securities
Only mandatory if corpus exceeds INR 500 crore
Mandatory for all AIFs; each scheme can have a different custodian to segregate assets and liabilities
Optional; trustees can perform custodial functions internally

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 13.7.2, under existing SEBI regulations, appointing a custodian is mandatory for ALL AIFs. Each scheme can have a different custodian to segregate assets and liabilities of that scheme. Regulation 20(11) requires sponsors/managers of AIFs to appoint a custodian for safekeeping of securities. The Trap: Historically, only Cat III / >INR 500 cr Cat I-II needed custodian, but that threshold has since been removed — all AIFs now need a custodian. Trustees cannot substitute for a custodian. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A surface-recalls this. XIX-C drills into custodian functions (tax certificate, post-trade corporate actions, leverage-breach reporting for Cat III). Manager's Pro-Tip: Appoint the custodian before date of first investment — waiting till investments start creates a dangerous gap. Negotiate SLAs around tax certificate issuance (FY-end rush is real).
